topic: How does orbital configuration affect the feasibility of frequency reuse ratios in flexible beam allocation for HTS systems?
response: Orbital configuration affects the feasibility of frequency reuse ratios in flexible beam allocation for HTS systems by enabling or limiting the spatial separation between beams. In geostationary (GEO) orbits, high-throughput satellites (HTS) can achieve narrower beams with frequency reuse across multiple beams, increasing capacity and decreasing costs per Mb/s.
reference_context: The Context mentions that HTS systems are launched in GEO, Low Earth Orbit (LEO), and Medium Earth Orbit (MEO) orbits. It also states that HTS can achieve 20 times more throughput than traditional fixed satellite services.
